title: Stirling LK517 Memorial, Shildon Cricket Club
location_name: Hackworth Road, Shildon Cricket Club, Shildon, County Durham, England
memorial_details: Memorial bench with plaque at the boundary of Shildon Cricket Club, Hackworth Road. The plaque carries a verse by A. E. Housman. Memorial erected principally through the efforts of local man Keith Robson. The crash site itself is about a mile away, at West Thickley off Spout Lane between Middridge and Shildon.
inscription: Here dead we lie because we did not choose to live and shame the land from which we sprung
crew_summary: All seven killed when the aircraft broke up in storm clouds and dived into the ground at West Thickley on 31 May 1944.
narrative:
LK517 took off from RAF Wigsley on the afternoon of 31 May 1944 on a routine navigational and bombing exercise. At approximately 16:45 a prisoner-of-war camp garrison engineer near Darlington heard the aircraft and noted from its sounds that it appeared to be in difficulties.

The aircraft crashed between Middridge and Shildon in Store Fields, off Spout Lane, at West Thickley. The Court of Inquiry concluded that the pilot had most likely lost control in storm clouds and entered an uncontrolled dive. The subsequent violent recovery attempt overstressed the airframe and the tail assembly failed in the air. The aircraft broke up before impact, scattering wreckage across the fields. All seven men were killed.

Pilot P/O Stanley Raymond Wilson was from Heaton, Newcastle. The Housman verse on the memorial — from A Shropshire Lad — is a spare and appropriate choice for men who died in training, far from any enemy, while preparing to defend the country.

crew.name: Stanley Raymond Wilson
crew.burial_location: Ryker and Heaton Cemetery, Newcastle upon Tyne

contributor: Keith Binley, Bomber Command Memorial Register
community_connection: Memorial researched and erected by Keith Robson, a local man. Shildon Cricket Club hosts the memorial at their ground boundary on Hackworth Road.
